associationClusters.association: China's export share and high-value manufacturing competitiveness are rising while global firms still struggle to replicate China's supplier, labor, power and logistics ecosystem. Search only after this hub signal for measurable second-order beneficiaries in automation, industrial power, logistics and supplier localization.

A stronger yuan changes landed input costs and FX translation while record gold imports show one concrete import response. Search for companies with large USD-linked input costs or liabilities and RMB revenue, while treating export-heavy firms as possible losers.

AI demand remains strong, Alibaba is expanding the full stack and targeting >20GW data-center capacity by 2032, while China-generalist reporting says AIDC delivery has compressed from years to months and stress is propagating into power and cooling. Test power-conversion and infrastructure suppliers for already-realized order/revenue conversion and financing/capex risk.

Recycling capacity materially exceeds compliant feedstock. The economic question is not 'recycling growth' but which operators control captive/contracted feedstock or closed-loop material flows and which standalone capacity is stranded.

Vanke-specific bank support and Beijing's presale/ready-home reform both point to a shift in the property funding model. Separate temporary liquidity support from durable business-model advantage; test cash-rich developers, construction-finance implications and supplier/customer credit risk.

Lower magnet exports and elevated supply-risk pricing may shift bargaining power upstream while hurting downstream manufacturers. Verify actual licensing/export volumes, company quota/resource exposure and downstream pass-through before any stock selection.

denominator.note: All six clusters remain in the denominator even if they yield no A-share selection.
